snippet.title: What Happens When Governments Spend Too Much?
snippet.description:
Fiscal policy can push the economy forward—or slow it down. In this short, we explain the difference between expansionary and contractionary fiscal policy:

Expansionary policy = more spending and lower taxes to boost growth

Used during recessions to create jobs and stimulate demand

Contractionary policy = higher taxes or reduced spending to slow inflation

Used when economies are “overheating” with too much demand

The challenge: choosing the right tool at the right time

Fiscal policy is like driving the economy—step on the gas, or hit the brakes. Get it wrong, and the economy can spiral into crisis.

snippet.title: The Secret Deal That Carved Up the Middle East
snippet.description:
In May 1916, two men met quietly in London. They took a map, drew a line across it, and divided an entire region between their two empires. The people who lived there were not consulted.

This is Episode 3 of World History — The Untold Story.

00:00 Cover
0:20 Opening Hook — London and Paris, May 1916
1:01 The World Before — The Ottoman Empire and the Eastern Question
2:08 The Promise — Hussein-McMahon and the Arab Revolt
3:00 The Secret Deal — Sykes-Picot signed in secret
4:03 The Betrayal Revealed — The Bolsheviks expose the agreement, 1917
4:40 The Map That Followed — Artificial borders, divided communities
5:39 The Long Shadow — A century of consequences
6:32 Closing — The borders drawn by people who never had to live inside them

The Sykes-Picot Agreement is often described as the source of everything that has gone wrong in the Middle East. That is too simple. But what is not debatable is this: two men divided a region they did not come from, on behalf of empires whose interests had nothing to do with the people already living there. And they did it in secret, while simultaneously telling those same people something entirely different.

This is the third chapter in our series on the untold stories that shaped world history.

snippet.title: How Greed Built a Market — And Then Destroyed It
snippet.description:
On the morning of October 24th, 1929, a man named Richard Whitney walked onto the floor of the New York Stock Exchange and placed a desperate order. He was trying to stop a panic. It did not work.

By the end of that week, the most chaotic financial collapse in American history was underway. But the crash of 1929 was not simply about greed. It was about a system built with no safeguards — one designed to amplify gains, with nothing to slow it down on the way back.

This is the untold story of how the Roaring Twenties turned into the Great Depression, and why the real lesson of 1929 has never fully been learned.

snippet.title: Could Hyperinflation Happen Again?
snippet.description:
We know hyperinflation from history—but could it strike modern economies too?
In this short, we explore whether hyperinflation is still possible today:

Why strong central banks make it less likely in advanced economies

How excessive debt and poor policy can still trigger risks

Countries like Argentina and Turkey facing inflation crises today

Why trust in currency is the foundation of stability

snippet.description:
Why Having Cash Is More Powerful Than You Think

What if the real power in personal finance isn’t investing, credit, or income—but cash?

In this video, we explore the hidden power of liquidity and why having cash reserves can completely change how you make decisions about work, money, and opportunity. Most financial advice focuses on investing for long-term growth, but it rarely explains the strategic role of cash.

During economic crises—like the 2008 Financial Crisis or the COVID-19 Market Crash 2020—one pattern repeats again and again:
people with liquidity buy assets at historic discounts, while those without liquidity are forced to sell.

Cash is not just for emergencies.
Cash creates leverage.

It allows you to negotiate better salaries, walk away from bad deals, handle financial shocks, and act when opportunities appear. Without cash reserves, people operate in survival mode—making decisions driven by urgency instead of strategy.

In this video, we break down:

• Why cash improves decision-making and reduces financial stress
• The hidden “poverty premium” that makes being broke more expensive
• How liquidity changes power dynamics at work and in negotiations
• Why investors with cash win during market crashes
• The three stages of building financial security through savings
• How to structure an emergency fund and opportunity fund

Understanding liquidity is one of the most important financial lessons most people never learn until it's too late.

Cash doesn’t just protect you.
Cash gives you options.

And options are where real financial power begins.

Juliana is forced to confront the weight of her past when she comes face-to-face with her imprisoned daughter, while Haziqah struggles with helplessness after receiving devastating news about her son.

Throughout human history, what we’ve called progress has often led to unintended consequences -collapsing civilizations and creating new crises. Today, those same patterns are playing out on a global scale.

Featuring insights from leading thinkers, activists, economists, and scientists, the film examines “progress traps”- innovations that solve short-term problems but create long-term risks. As these traps become embedded in our technology, economy, and way of life, the question becomes urgent:

Can humanity change course before history repeats itself?

snippet.title: Boring History for Sleep: The Birth of Accounting & The House of Wisdom
snippet.description:
Travel back in time to the cradle of civilization and the bustling markets of the Islamic Golden Age in this relaxing history sleep story. Tonight, we explore the surprisingly profound history of accounting—from the clay tablets of Ancient Sumer to the House of Wisdom in Baghdad.

We will trace the journey of knowledge from Mesopotamia to Rome, through the waqfs of the Islamic world, and finally to Renaissance Europe with Fibonacci and Luca Pacioli.

Let the quiet details of ledgers, merchants, and ancient libraries soothe you into a deep slumber. This educational documentary is designed to be low-stimulation and informative, perfect for quieting the mind and helping you fall asleep fast.

-The origins of writing and accounting in Ancient Mesopotamia.
-Roman and Persian administrative systems.
-The House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma) in Baghdad.
-The invention of Algebra and the adoption of Hindu-Arabic numerals.
-Islamic commercial law, partnerships, and the Waqf system.

snippet.title: The Simple Money Routine That will Change your Finances
snippet.description:
The Simple Money Routine That will Change your Finances

For generations, building wealth followed a simple routine.
Work hard. Spend less than you earn. Save consistently. Let time do the rest.

In 1962, a factory worker could follow this routine and retire with dignity. A modest salary, a paid-off home, and steady savings were enough to build a stable financial life.

But something changed.

Today, millions of people work harder than ever, read the books, download budgeting apps, and watch endless personal finance advice… yet still struggle to build real wealth.

Why?

Because the economic environment has changed dramatically. Wages, credit systems, inflation, asset prices, and consumer culture have reshaped the rules of money. The same habits that once built wealth can now leave people stuck financially.

In this video, we break down the simple money routine that still works today — and why most people never follow it. This is not a motivational speech or a “get rich quick” strategy.

It’s a clear look at how financial systems actually work — and the simple routine that has quietly built wealth across generations.

Because the truth is simple:

Wealth is rarely built through dramatic moves.

It’s built through boring, consistent routines that compound over time.

If you understand the system early enough, you can stop fighting it — and start using it.
